title: Bounded simulation of a walk
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean input and work-tape symbols, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, let $bits$ be a Boolean encoding of the selectors of $M$, and let $P$ be an input-head position for $y$. For any proposed output state $oq$, output register $r$, auxiliary tape content $\tau_C$ and position $z_C$, natural number $v$, Boolean word $w$, configuration $c$ of $M$ on $x$, and tag $b$, if $w$ has counter value $v$ and $b$ correctly marks the boundary position of $c$'s input head, then the machine constructed from $M$, started in its waiting-decision state with these data, halts within $(v+1)(2|w|+3)$ steps and outputs the single bit that answers the decoded selector using $oq$, $r$, and the symbols read from $c$ after $v$ simulated selector-walk steps.
hypotheses_covered: M is a finite-state Turing machine over Boolean symbols
x and y are Boolean words
bits is a Boolean selector encoding
P is a valid input-head position for y
oq is an optional state and r is an output register
τC is an auxiliary tape content and zC an integer position
v is a natural number and w is a Boolean word with ctrVal(w)=v
c is a configuration of M on x
b correctly tags c's input-head boundary position
